name: aura
blurb: Effortless cool or presence; smooth moves earn "aura points", cringe loses them
title: Aura Meaning: What Does Aura Mean in Slang?
description: In slang, aura means effortless cool or presence. It grew out of sports talk and went viral on TikTok in May 2024 with jokes about gaining or losing aura points.
h1: What does aura mean in slang?
answer: In slang, aura means a cool, confident presence: someone with aura seems impressive without trying, like an athlete who stays calm in a big moment. Online, people give made-up scores to everyday moments, "+1000 aura" for something smooth and "-1000 aura" for something embarrassing. The sense grew out of sports talk in the early 2020s, and the "aura points" format went viral on TikTok from May 2024.

body: The standard English word aura means a special atmosphere or quality a person seems to give off. The slang sense keeps that idea but narrows it to coolness: style, calm confidence, the feeling that someone is a bit untouchable. It is close to rizz, but without the flirting.
Aura is treated like a score you can gain or lose. Doing something effortlessly impressive earns aura; tripping on stage, sending a text to the wrong person or trying too hard costs it.

head: Date
Event
rows: Fans start describing athletes and performers who shine under pressure as having "aura".
On 1 May a TikToker posts the first known "aura points" video, scoring how much aura he lost; school-themed versions get tens of millions of plays within weeks.
"How many aura points did I lose when..." becomes a common template on TikTok, X and Instagram.
"Aura farming", deliberately acting cool to gain aura, goes global with a viral clip of a young boat dancer at Indonesia's Pacu Jalur boat race.

ul: "He hit the game-winner and didn't even celebrate. Insane aura."
"I waved back at someone who was waving at the person behind me. -5000 aura."
"Teacher said 'nice' to my answer in front of everyone, +1000 aura."
"Stop aura farming, we all saw you check if anyone was watching."

body: Aura is playful and mostly used by teens and young adults, often with exaggerated numbers. It is a compliment when you say someone "has aura", and light teasing when you take points away. It is not a spiritual or new-age meaning here, though the word still has that sense in other contexts.

faq.a: Made-up scores for how cool or embarrassing a moment was, as in "+1000 aura" or "-1000 aura". The format went viral on TikTok in May 2024.
Deliberately acting cool or mysterious to look impressive, like posing or staying dramatically calm. It is often said teasingly.

faq.q: Is aura the same as rizz?
faq.a: Not quite. Rizz is charm aimed at attracting someone romantically; aura is general coolness and presence.
